messages.subject: Resources for understanding "error=TRUE"
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

I am using CTMM for estimating home ranges using satellite telemetry on an avian species. I see that you use the GPS turtle dataset for the Telemetry Error vignette on the ctmm github page and so I'm not sure how to apply the error=TRUE function to Argos data. First of all, when I download data from Argos, I do not see the columns that you specify for the pelican dataset (COV and VAR). Instead, I have the following:

Error radius
Semi-major axis
Semi-minor axis
Ellipse orientation
GDOP

Here are my questions. 1) Which of these columns do I need for model fitting with Argos telemetry error and how do I tell CTMM to do so? 2) Should I be getting CI estimates for the error in my summary(FIT) results? and 3) Do you have a resource that explains how the error is accounted for in the model fitting process? I am needing to explain this for a poster presentation about my methods for estimating these home ranges and I have to admit that I'm a little lost here.

Thanks so much for your support,
Karina

messages.subject: 3D fish data inquiry
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dr. Chris and anyone else with insight,

First thank you for your efforts & extensive resources, all very helpful and very much appreciated. Please pardon if I haven't gotten to everything yet and am missing something obvious.

I have been trying to analyze 3D acoustic telemetry data of fish from an artificial reef with CTMM and have had success in executing the main functions and producing 2D models/plots, but am struggling with incorporating depth which is a crucial component. I have found some threads on VMM from 2021, but first am curious if you have any other updated recommendations for depth?

I also am curious if this package is most appropriate for my data, given the following: the fish are constrained by the sea floor (~25 m), positions are calculated at a minimum interval rate of 10 secs (so ~140,000 events in a month, up to 7-9 months of data across 19 individuals), the fish are highly residential, and when filtered by DOP < 1, the data is inherently constrained to a ~200m x ~150m space. So home range is already bounded but my main research questions lie in how they are using specific parts of the habitat and how this use changes temporally.

Thanks in advance,
-Clark

messages.subject: Re: Resources for understanding "error=TRUE"
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karina,

For now you can rename the ellipse columns to "Argos.orientation", "Argos semi-major" and "Argos semi-minor" and that should import the error ellipses correctly. In the next update, I will have your original column names correctly identified.
No, the model just assumes the Argos error ellipses are the true covariance parameters. Something more accurate would be a little complicated to implement, because you have a mixture of two error distributions for the two polar orbit paths, like "\" and "/" that together give you a "X" shaped error distribution, which makes for many unknown parameters to consider.
There is a pre-print that explains the reasoning behind the modeling choices - and, specifically, not freely fitting the error variance to tracking data: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2020.06.12.130195v2.full
But the model structure itself is the same kind of state-space model as has been used for decades, such as in Devin Johnson's crawl package.
Best,
Chris

messages.subject: ctmm workshop at AWMS 2024 (Australia)
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

There will be a 4-day continuous-time movement modeling (ctmm) workshop in coordination with the Australian Wildlife Management Society (AWMS) 2024 conference:  https://awms.org.au/conference/. The AWMS conference will run Dec. 3-5 in Fremantle, Perth, and the ctmm workshop will take place the following week Dec. 9-12 at Murdoch University, Perth.

There will soon by a link to a registration page at https://awms.org.au/conference/, but in the interim you can email Roy Teale (r...@biota.net.au) with an expression of interest, and he will let you know when registration becomes available. The location is confirmed and the cost will be approximately $800 AUD.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject_clean: Trouble shooting data problems for RSF
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

During Animove 2024, you mentioned that the rsf.fit would be able to handle choppy data and irregular sampling at different levels. I'm currently having trouble with it because of problematic individuals.

I'm attaching the code I'm using (file called 3. SEO_RSF_multiple.R), and the problem I have is when using akde (line 102 of the code). The logic is that some individuals are not able to have a proper convergence of the model due to the amount of data (or at least that is what I think).

Upon inspection (using the other code I'm attaching, SEO_diagnostic.R), based on your suggestions online <https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/articles/variogram.html>, the variograms do not show good data.

I followed Bjorn's code, which I'm also attaching in case you need the context of what I was trying to do.

The raster files can be downloaded directly from this Google Drive folder <https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/14mjtw1gXRPWRBAGnABPprCPD3rpWHOjz?usp=sharing>.

So, my main question is how to troubleshoot within CTMM to either filter out these individuals or use the poor information these individuals provide.

Thank you so much for any advice or insight.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris.

I have run into a problem when trying to calculate pairwise proximity and distance metrics between two individuals of a different species.

In short, the problem I have is that their ctmm's have different projections because I analysed them seperately. I know that you can change the projection of a telemetry object, but is it possible to change the projection of a ctmm object?

This is what I tried to do to rectify the issue (as what would work with a telemetry object)

test_ctmm <- list(pike_muddyfoot_ctmm_fits$F59880, roach_muddyfoot_ctmm_fits$F59707)

ctmm::projection( test_ctmm   ) <-ctmm::median( test_ctmm )

Error in getMethod("median", CLASS) : Cannot find method median for class ctmm

I am assuming that I am unable to change the projection once the movement has been modelled.

Some context about the data I am working with. My data is from a multi-experimental lake study where we tracked 3 different species of fish (2 prey: roach (30 individuals) and perch (30 individuals), 1 predator: northern pike (6 individuals)) in each lake. Median sampling interval for each species ~4secs, tracked over ~36 days. I'm interested in estimating the interaction rates, and possible predation events,  between predator and prey.

As you can imagine, I have a lot of location data, and running the ctmm's took a very long time, so if I can avoid re-running these, that would be ideal.

Thanks for your time
Marcus

messages.subject: Speed of an animal that is stationary
messages.subject_clean: Speed of an animal that is stationary
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris and the rest of the group!

I have started using ctmm to estimate the instantaneous speed of hedgehogs tagged with GPS. I want to analyze their nocturnal activity pattern and potential differences between males and females. The GPS devices (I-gotU) record the individual's position every 3 minutes, only during the nights. I have estimated the error of the devices using the uere.fit function, utilizing 2 of the GPS units at two different locations.

The estimated instantaneous speed decreases to approximately constant values during time intervals that appear to be periods when the hedgehog is stationary. However, this minimum speed is not zero but rather a higher value. As an example, I have attached an image corresponding to an individual tracked over 7 nights. The fitted model (using ctmm.guess and ctmm.select based on the script from Noonan et al. 2019) is "OUF anisotropic error." In this graph, the minimum speed is approximately 65 m/hour.

Graph all nigths attached

Example of a graph for one of the nights (night 5):

 Graph nigth 5 attached

I think that this minimum speed is likely a result of the model not being able to completely eliminate the GPS error when the animal is stationary and possibly hidden in a spot where the signal reception is poor. I would appreciate it if you could confirm whether this is the case. I would also like to ask if it would be correct to adjust the speeds for each night by subtracting the minimum speed for that night so that the speed when the animal is stationary would approximate zero.

For the case of night 5 mentioned earlier, the graph would become the following with that correction:

Graph nigth 5 corrected attached

Thank you very much!

Germán López
